result.summary: The residential environment lacks continuous sidewalks, forcing pedestrians to share the roadway with vehicles. While a marked crosswalk is present, it lacks curb ramps and is partially obscured by a large parked vehicle, creating significant visibility issues.

hazards.name: Lack of Sidewalks
hazards.description: Pedestrians have no dedicated walkway and must walk in the street or on unpaved surfaces.
hazards.location_in_image: Throughout the foreground and midground along the road edges.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicle
hazards.description: A large delivery truck is parked near the intersection, blocking sightlines between drivers and pedestrians at the crosswalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Center-left, white truck parked on the shoulder.

hazards.name: Incomplete Crossing Infrastructure
hazards.description: The marked crosswalk lacks curb ramps and connects to grass rather than a paved sidewalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the intersection.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Construct paved sidewalks on both sides of the street to separate pedestrians from vehicular traffic.

interventions.title: Daylighting at Crosswalks
interventions.description: Implement parking restrictions near the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install detectable warning surfaces and sloped ramps at the crosswalk to ensure accessibility for all users.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a marked zebra crosswalk and warning signage in a residential setting, but lacks connecting sidewalks and ADA-compliant curb ramps. Pedestrians are forced to navigate grassy verges or the roadway to access the crossing, which is further compromised by potential sightline obstructions from mature trees.

hazards.name: Missing Sidewalks
hazards.description: No paved walkways exist to lead pedestrians to or from the marked crosswalk, forcing them onto the grass or roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Both sides of the roadway

hazards.name: Lack of Curb Ramps
hazards.description: The crosswalk terminates at unpaved, non-level surfaces, creating a barrier for people with disabilities.
hazards.location_in_image: Ends of the crosswalk

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Mature trees and vegetation near the intersection may block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image near the curve

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Construct paved sidewalks on at least one side of the street to provide a dedicated space for pedestrians.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install detectable warning surfaces and sloped ramps at the crosswalk landings.

interventions.title: Vegetation Management
interventions.description: Trim or remove low-hanging branches and shrubs near the crossing to improve visibility (daylighting).

result.summary: The image shows a residential intersection with a marked zebra crosswalk and curb ramps. While the environment is leafy and appears low-speed, the pavement within the crossing is degraded and dense vegetation may limit visibility at the corners.

hazards.name: Degraded Pavement
hazards.description: The asphalt within the marked crosswalk is cracked and uneven, creating a trip hazard for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground, within the zebra stripes.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Dense trees and bushes at the corner may obscure pedestrians from the view of approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Left and center background at the intersection corner.

interventions.title: Pavement Repair
interventions.description: Resurface the intersection and crosswalk area to provide a smooth, level walking surface.

interventions.title: Vegetation Management
interventions.description: Trim back trees and shrubs near the intersection to improve sight triangles for both drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Crossing Signage
interventions.description: Install 'Pedestrian Crossing' warning signs to alert drivers to the presence of the crosswalk.

result.summary: The intersection features high-visibility zebra crosswalks and a stop sign, but lacks dedicated sidewalks and ADA-compliant curb ramps. Dense vegetation at the corners creates potential sightline obstructions between drivers and pedestrians.
